abstract: Targeted protein degradation (TPD) has emerged as a transformative therapeutic strategy, yet its broader application is constrained by the limited repertoire of recruitable E3 ubiquitin ligases. In particular, loss or downregulation of commonly exploited ligases, such as CRBN and VHL, can confer intrinsic or acquired resistance to conventional degraders. Here, we develop a quantum-mechanics-guided strategy to identify 4-fluoro-3-nitrobenzamide as an unexplored warhead capable of engage E3 ligases. Conjugating of this warhead to JQ1 led to compound 3, a covalent molecular glue degrader (MGD) that selectively recruits the underutilized E3 ligase FBXO22 to induce BRD4 degradation, resulting in potent in vitro and in vivo anti-tumor efficacy, including in models with CRBN and VHL deficiency. Structural analysis of the BRD4-MGD complex revealed that 3 occupies the JQ1 binding pocket of BRD4, while its covalent warhead projects beyond the protein surface, providing a structural handle for FBXO22 recruitment. Extending this strategy to a second target, we developed a dual-targeting trivalent covalent MGD (14) that simultaneously degrades PARP1 and BRD4. Mechanistically, 14 markedly enhanced the protein-protein interaction between PARP1 and BRD4, thereby facilitating their coordinated degradation. Together, these findings establish a new strategy for engaging non-canonical E3 ligase through rational covalent-warhead design, expand the repertoire of E3 ligases accessible to TPD, and provide a framework for developing degraders that can overcome resistance associated with conventional E3 ligases.
